children: Richelieu Hardware is investing more than 15 million Canadian dollars ($10.8 million) to upgrade its distribution center in Drummondville, Quebec.
The Canadian specialty hardware store said Thursday that the investment will go toward expanding the size of its facility to 180,000 square feet from the current 40,000.
Richelieu aims to increase its distribution capacity to meet growing demand throughout the province.

"By expanding our distribution center from 40,000 to 180,000 square feet, we are significantly strengthening our ability to serve our customers while continuing to invest in Quebec," said Chief Executive Richard Lord.
The company expects the new facilities to be up and running by spring of next year, it said.

At the same time, the company is also expanding its presence in the U.S., where it also has a significant footprint. Late Wednesday, Richelieu announced the acquisition of the door hardware and components division of Penrod Company.
